security_audit.summary: The skill has a legitimate media workflow, but it combines network providers, credential loading, filesystem caches, bundled binaries, and extensive local command execution. Several static hits are false positives from Markdown, tests, or JavaScript template literals, but critical risks remain in shell-backed local model execution, remote installer guidance, parent .env loading, and cross-project global cache reuse.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is documented as curl piped to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the pipe-to-shell command with signed release downloads, package-manager installation, and checksum verification steps.

remediation.issue: Local model commands are template-filled and executed through a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Use execFileSync or spawn with argv arrays, quote nothing through a shell, and validate every prompt, path, and numeric argument before execution.

remediation.issue: The HeyGen helper auto-loads parent .env files into process.env.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit credential sources, stop walking parent directories by default, and never import unrelated .env values into the process.

remediation.issue: Global media cache can expose prompts and assets across projects.
remediation.suggestion: Partition the cache by workspace or organization, redact prompt text from global listings, and require explicit confirmation before global reuse.

remediation.issue: A nested Codex CLI run receives user media intent as a prompt.
remediation.suggestion: Constrain nested agent execution with a fixed tool-only contract, remove no-confirmation wording, and reject intents that include instructions to alter files or run commands.

remediation.issue: Bundled MP3 assets are binary files outside static source review.
remediation.suggestion: Publish hashes, licenses, provenance, and malware-scanning results for each audio asset before marketplace publication.

remediation.issue: Telemetry is enabled unless users opt out.
remediation.suggestion: Make telemetry opt-in for marketplace distribution, document exact fields sent, and keep network failure non-blocking.

content.value_statement: Media-heavy projects need consistent assets, captions, and reuse records. This skill resolves media into local files and tracks provenance for agent workflows.
actual_capabilities: Resolve background music, sound effects, images, icons, and voice assets into project .media folders.
Search HeyGen catalogs and use local or CLI-based generation fallbacks when configured.
Create voiceover audio metadata with durations and word timestamps for captions.
Transcribe media, build transcript-based cuts, and apply audio ducking recipes.
Register assets in manifests and surface reusable project or global cache candidates.
Ingest local files or direct public media URLs and freeze them into the project ledger.
limitations: Some providers require external CLIs, local model installs, or user-owned API credentials.
The skill runs local scripts and subprocesses, so users should review permissions before use.
Bundled MP3 sound effects are binary assets and require separate provenance review.
The global cache can surface assets from earlier projects unless reuse is checked carefully.

best_practices: Review reuse candidates before importing global cache assets into a client project.
Use local-only mode when network providers or paid cloud tools are not approved.

anti_patterns: Do not run remote installer commands from documentation without verifying the source and checksum.
Do not reuse a global brand asset unless the entity and project context match exactly.
Do not pass untrusted text into local model command templates without reviewing shell behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill require HeyGen credentials?
faq.answer: No. Some HeyGen retrieval and TTS paths need credentials, but local and bundled fallbacks exist for several media types.

faq.question: Can it work offline?
faq.answer: Yes, local-only mode skips network providers and uses project assets, global cache entries, and installed local tools.

faq.question: What files does it create?
faq.answer: It creates project media files, manifest records, index files, temporary processing files, and optional global cache entries.

faq.question: Does it send telemetry?
faq.answer: The skill includes opt-out telemetry for usage events. Users can disable it with documented environment variables.

faq.question: Can it generate images?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use local mflux when installed or a Codex image generation path when configured.

faq.question: Is every bundled sound effect reviewed?
faq.answer: The bundle contains MP3 files. Marketplaces should keep hashes, license records, and malware review results for those binaries.
